entities.label: Idea
entities.summary:
Theatre art is an ancient and widespread form of storytelling that has shaped human culture for millennia. Originating in prehistoric civilizations, it evolved into a sophisticated art form in ancient Greece, where the Greeks developed the concept of drama and tragedy. The Greeks' theatrical innovations were later adopted by the Romans, who further refined the craft.

   By the 17th century, European theatre had become an integral part of the performing arts scene, with famous playwrights like William Shakespeare and Molière creating iconic works that continue to be performed today. As the Industrial Revolution transformed urban landscapes, theatres began to sprout up in cities across the globe, catering to the growing middle class.

   Today, theatre art remains a vibrant and diverse global phenomenon, with new forms of performance and storytelling emerging all the time. From avant-garde experimental works to traditional folk performances, theatre continues to captivate audiences worldwide.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Theatre art has played a significant role in shaping Western cultural identity, influencing literature, politics, and social change throughout history.
